title: Why does keeping timestamps cut a clip 1.4 seconds early?
fullTitle: FFmpeg -copyts with -ss: a Cut at 3.5 s Starts at Frame 21 When the File Clock Starts at 1.4 s

scenes.narration: You cut with dash s s three point five and add dash copyts. What is kept, and which frame comes first? A hundred frames that name themselves. Synthetic, f f m peg six point one point one.
captions: Cut at 3.5 s, keep the timestamps.
What is kept, and which frame is first?

scenes.narration: Ten frames a second, a keyframe every second. Reader one: ffprobe, start time and packets. Reader two: the decoded pictures, and the decoder's own clock. They agree.
captions: ffprobe packets and decoded pictures agree.

scenes.narration: Without copyts, the cut restarts the clock: frame thirty five at zero, in mp four and m k v, with the option before or after the input. T s starts at one point four: its muxer adds that.
captions: Frame 35 starts at 0 in mp4 and mkv.
The ts muxer starts its clock at 1.4 s.

scenes.narration: Copyts before the input keeps the source clock: frame thirty five stays at three point five. In t s the muxer adds one point four: frame forty at six point eight, not five point four. Start at zero gives five point four.
captions: mp4, mkv: 3.5 s, the source clock.
ts: 6.8 s, 1.4 s more than the source.

scenes.narration: Copyts after the input: the cut is measured on the file's own clock. A file that starts at one point four seconds is cut one point four seconds early: frame twenty one, not thirty five. Same in an m k v shifted to one point four; not in a t s from zero. Start at zero repairs it.
captions: A file that starts at 0 is not affected.

scenes.narration: Which frame is first? Re-encoded, mp four and m k v land exactly. T s lands on the next keyframe: three point two seconds starts at frame forty. Stream copy in m k v starts at the keyframe before; in mp four an edit list hides it: seventy packets, sixty five frames.

So: copyts keeps the clock, and ss after the input then counts on that clock. Add start at zero, or subtract the offset. Check the first frame. Not tested: other builds, B frames, audio, real footage.
captions: Not tested: other builds, B frames, audio, real footage.
Check the first frame, not the timestamps.
